ov: Compact, heavily built game birds of the Northern Hemisphere, from arctic tundra to pine forest, moorland and mountains. Their feathered legs and toes help them walk on snow and burrow into it for shelter. Many males display in groups (leks) at dawn and dusk.

why.et: A game bird: hunters kill millions each year for food and sport.

rg: Temperate and subarctic North America, Europe and Asia, as far north as 83°N.
df: Buds, catkins, leaves and twigs make up over 95% of adults’ food; chicks eat mostly insects.
fx: In all but two or three species, males mate with several females.
Grouse make up a large share of the animal biomass in the Arctic and subarctic.
